verify_method: Ported to schema (Phase 0). Statuses below are the corpus author's original codes at load time; Phase 1 verify pass to follow.

claims.claim: About one in four Nebraskans experiences a behavioral health issue each year, yet provider shortages and long wait times leave many unable to access care.
claims.source: BHECN (Behavioral Health Education Center of Nebraska), UNMC — Licensed Behavioral Health Workforce Report 2025 / 2026 Behavioral Health Workforce Capacity Report.
claims.expiry: BHECN publishes annually; refresh from unmc.edu/bhecn.

claims.claim: Nebraska's licensed behavioral health workforce grew 49% from 2010 to 2024 — yet demand continues to outpace supply, and Nebraska remains the only state longitudinally tracking this workforce.
claims.source: BHECN, 2026 Behavioral Health Workforce Capacity Report (released May 2026); unmc.edu/bhecn.
claims.expiry: Refresh with the next annual BHECN capacity report.
red_team_flags: Workforce growth (49%) and persistent shortage are not contradictory — pair them so a reviewer reads 'growing but still insufficient,' not a self-cancelling stat.

claims.claim: Nationally in 2023, 39.7% of high school students experienced persistent feelings of sadness or hopelessness, 20.4% seriously considered attempting suicide, and 9.5% attempted suicide.
claims.source: CDC, Youth Risk Behavior Survey, United States, 2023 (MMWR Supplement 73(4), Oct 2024).
claims.expiry: YRBS runs on a 2-year cycle; refresh with the 2025 YRBS (~2026 release).

claims.claim: Nebraska-specific youth behavioral-health figures (state-weighted YRBS or NRPFSS, including Douglas/Sarpy county coverage).
claims.source: NE DHHS YRBS results portal; fallback: Nebraska Risk and Protective Factor Student Survey (NRPFSS).
red_team_flags: Nebraska's YRBS participation/weighting varies by cycle — confirm whether 2023 state-weighted data exist before citing. NRPFSS has stronger county-level (Douglas/Sarpy) coverage.

claims.claim: Only about 20% of children with mental or behavioral disorders are identified and receive services from a specialized provider.
claims.source: CDC (2013). Refresh candidate: Whitney & Peterson (2019), JAMA Pediatrics — NSCH analysis (~half of children with a treatable MH disorder receive treatment).
claims.expiry: CDC 2013 vintage — already used in Connections materials. Refresh with the current NSCH treatment-gap figure before reusing in federal proposals.
red_team_flags: Vintage: 2013 figure. A knowledgeable federal reviewer will know the newer NSCH analyses (Whitney & Peterson 2019: roughly half of children with a treatable MH disorder receive treatment). Refresh before export.

claims.claim: HRSA Mental Health Health Professional Shortage Area (HPSA) designations across the 16 southwest Iowa counties Project Harmony serves.
red_team_flags: Most SW Iowa counties carry whole-county MH HPSA designations; county-by-county designation IDs strengthen HRSA and rural proposals. Pull the current designation IDs.
